Marisa.notes: 5f extra recovery on whiff; 2nd active frame is omitted on hit/block (when combined with the extra whiff recovery, the total frame count is 6f longer on whiff compared to hit/block); releasing the button on frames 5-16 results in uncharged version with 3f startup; short range but excellent combo and pressure tool; meaty connect does not give extra frame advantage; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state

Marisa.name: Ponte Milvio
Marisa.notes: Side switch; after throwing opponent into corner, can Drive Rush for strong strike/throw mixup; DR~5[HP] trades with reversal 4f normals for a high-damage trade combo; meaty options are much weaker after normal dash (no throw, limited conversions on hit); a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Marisa.name: Back Taunt
Marisa.notes: "This will be fun! *crack*"

Marisa.name: Standing Heavy Kick
Marisa.notes: Can hold button 17f for improved properties; solid poke with good hitbox priority; Punish Counter puts opponent into free juggle state; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; extends a hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles

Marisa.name: Marisa Style (HK)
Marisa.notes: Releasing the button on frames 5-13 results in uncharged version with 10f startup; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; Punish Counter causes free juggle state

Marisa.name: Standing Heavy Punch
Marisa.notes: Can hold button 21f for improved properties; strong whiff punish tool

Marisa.name: Marisa Style (HP)
Marisa.notes: 1f extra recovery on whiff; releasing the button on frames 7-17 results in uncharged version with 5f startup; great range and frame advantage for follow-up combos and pressure; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state

Marisa.name: Heavy Two Hitter
Marisa.notes: () refers to scaled damage after 5HP combo starter; 6f gap between hits on block (1f gap if starting from 5[HP]); grants a safe jump near the corner on a grounded hit or low-height juggle

Marisa.name: Standing Light Kick
Marisa.notes: At farther ranges, can only combo into SA2; special cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame; DR cancel is delayed until after 3rd recovery frame

Marisa.name: Standing Light Punch
Marisa.notes: Good neutral buffer into 5LP~LP Target Combo (requires at least a Counter-hit to combo); causes air reset if juggled into

Marisa.name: Light Two Hitter
Marisa.notes: Requires Counter-hit, Punish Counter, or Drive Rush 5LP to combo; 3f gap on block between hits that allows for a frame trap

Marisa.name: Standing Medium Kick
Marisa.notes: Good poke and Drive Rush starter

Marisa.name: Standing Medium Punch
Marisa.notes: 2f extra recovery on whiff; great hitbox and a strong buffer into 5MP~MP Target Combo

Marisa.name: Medium Two Hitter
Marisa.notes: Great pressure and bully tool from 5MP; true blockstring between hits; special/DR cancel is delayed until after 1st recovery frame

Marisa.name: Neutral Taunt
Marisa.notes: "I may need a second helping of you!"

Marisa.name: Phalanx
Marisa.notes: Cannot hit cross-up; hits 1f later vs. crouching opponents; leaves Marisa close enough to frame trap with 5LP~LP on block or use 5MP~MP without causing an air reset; can set up trade combos with 4f reversals using 5MP vs. stand block or 4HP vs. crouch block

Marisa.name: Phalanx
Marisa.notes: Cannot hit cross-up; hits 1f later vs. crouching opponents

Marisa.name: Phalanx
Marisa.notes: Cannot hit cross-up; hits 1f later vs. crouching opponents; leaves Marisa close enough to frame trap with 5LP~LP on block or use 5MP~MP without causing an air reset; can set up trade combos with 4f reversals using 5MP vs. stand block or 4HP vs. crouch block

Marisa.name: Phalanx
Marisa.notes: Sends opponent tumbling backward into OTG state; if opponent hits the corner, a low-height Wall Splat occurs (opponent is grounded and throwable, but strikes put them into juggle state); cannot hit cross-up; hits 1f later vs. crouching opponents; can set up trade combos with 4f reversals using 4HP vs. stand block or 6MP vs. crouch block

Marisa.name: Falx Crusher 1
Marisa.notes: Can hold button 21f for improved properties; has a hitconfirmable Target Combo follow-up; forces stand on hit

Marisa.name: Falx Crusher 2
Marisa.notes: Hitconfirmable ender after 6HK; delaying the input can create a frame trap up to 3f on block (no gap if starting from 6[HK]); puts opponent into limited juggle state; extremely powerful when juggled into (does not increase juggle count at all from DR~6HK)

Marisa.name: Falx Crusher 1 (Hold)
Marisa.notes: Releasing the button on frames 7-14 results in uncharged version with 7f startup (frames 15-20: 4f startup); has a hitconfirmable Target Combo follow-up; forces stand on hit; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; more range than uncharged version with excellent follow-up combos or block pressure; special/DR cancel is delayed until after 3rd active frame

Marisa.name: Love Tap (Block)
Marisa.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; 4f less hitstop on block compared to most Drive Reversals (changes the punish timing); see [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Reversal|Drive Reversal]].

Marisa.name: Love Tap (Recovery)
Marisa.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze; 4f less hitstop on block compared to most Drive Reversals (changes the punish timing); see [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Reversal|Drive Reversal]].

Marisa.name: Novacula 1
Marisa.notes: Strong forward movement and can link into light normals after Counter-hit, Punish Counter, or Drive Rush; has 2 hitconfirmable Target Combo follow-ups; useful link option out of DR~2MK due to its range

Marisa.name: Novacula Thrust
Marisa.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; if the opponent is standing, this ender is preferable for its corner carry and Super cancelability; Super cancel is delayed until after 3rd active frame

Marisa.name: Novacula Swipe
Marisa.notes: Low follow-up; true blockstring from 6MP, so an opponent mashing a crouching button after blocked 6MP will not be frame trapped; useful confirm if 6MP hits crouching opponent

Marisa.name: Forward Taunt
Marisa.notes: "Come on, the first hit's free."; active frames refer to armored period

Marisa.name: Secutor
Marisa.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Impact|Drive Impact]]. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

Marisa.name: Jumping Heavy Kick
Marisa.notes: Can hold button 20f for improved properties; lower body projectile invuln 10-21f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Marisa Style (j.HK)
Marisa.notes: Releasing the button on frames 7-19 results in uncharged version with 3f startup; causes spike knockdown; lower body projectile invuln 29-37f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Jumping Heavy Punch
Marisa.notes: Can hold button 20f for improved properties; causes spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; lower body projectile invuln 9-23f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Marisa Style (j.HP)
Marisa.notes: Releasing the button on frames 5-19 results in uncharged version with 5f startup; causes spike knockdown; lower body projectile invuln 28-37f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Jumping Light Kick
Marisa.notes: Cross-up; useful for safe jumps; can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead

Marisa.name: Jumping Light Punch
Marisa.notes: Quick air-to-air

Marisa.name: Jumping Medium Kick
Marisa.notes: Farthest reaching horizontal jump-in with good hitbox priority; lower body projectile invuln 8-25f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Jumping Medium Punch
Marisa.notes: Puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; lower body projectile invuln 7-21f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Volare Combo
Marisa.notes: Spike KD vs. airborne opponents

Marisa.name: Mounted Grace
Marisa.notes: Can use Drive Rush for a corner throw loop with 2f timing on standard characters; a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Marisa.name: Drive Parry
Marisa.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Parry|Drive Parry]]. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

Marisa.name: Drive Rush Cancel
Marisa.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Rush|Drive Rush]]; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

Marisa.name: Parry Drive Rush
Marisa.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Rush|Drive Rush]]; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.544 (min/throw), 1.903 (min/block), 3.081 (max/final DR frame)

Marisa.name: Caelum Arc
Marisa.notes: Can hit Cross-up; can hold button 20f for improved properties; causes spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; lower body projectile invuln 9f until land except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Marisa.name: Caelum Arc (Hold)
Marisa.notes: Can hit Cross-up; releasing the button on frames 5-19 results in uncharged version with 4f startup; causes spike knockdown; lower body projectile invuln 28f until land except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Rashid.name: Ysaar
Rashid.notes: No invincibility; puts opponent into limited juggle state; spawns a 5-hit Super projectile tornado; travels fullscreen on its own, and Rashid can kick it with 214P to make it travel faster (can also kick tornado in the opposite direction after a side switch); tornado remains active even if it disappears off-screen; creates Air Current that lasts until 120f after Super dissipates (enhances many of Rashid's moves); listed KD Advantage is from point blank connect; cannot use 236K Whirlwind Shot while Super is active; cannot gain Super Art gauge while the projectile hitbox is active

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; on block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); on hit, Rashid gets better KD Advantage on later active frames; opponent slides on the ground for great corner carry; can be affected by Air Current on frames 6-30

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike (Air Current)
Rashid.notes: Functions identically to enhanced 214MK; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; on hit/block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); opponent slides on the ground for great corner carry; Punish Counter tumble allows for a follow-up 214K for even more damage and corner carry

Rashid.name: Arabian Cyclone
Rashid.notes: Strike hitbox; spawns a tornado with 2 hits of projectile durability; first hit puts opponent into limited juggle state; the 2-hit tornado does not cause a knockdown on its own, and carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits if it connects; cancelable into 4K Wing Stroke or 6K Rolling Assault on frames 33-34; high active frame count makes it great for oki; 29f recovery is total time after the tornado's 2nd hit occurs; 24f recovery is total time after tornado disappears; advantage when canceled into 6K Roll: KD+43/+1

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit and side switches if the opponent is not cornered; on block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); on hit, Rashid gets better KD Advantage on later active frames; can be affected by Air Current on frames 6-29

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike (Air Current)
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit and side switches if the opponent is not cornered; on block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); on hit, Rashid gets better KD Advantage on later active frames

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit (can lead to follow-up juggles if well spaced); on block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); on hit, Rashid gets better KD Advantage on later active frames; can be affected by Air Current on frames 4-14; SA3 cancel occurs on hit only, allowing it to be freely buffered for extra damage

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike (Air Current)
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; on block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); on hit, Rashid gets better KD Advantage on later active frames; SA3 cancel occurs on hit only, allowing it to be freely buffered for extra damage

Rashid.name: Arabian Cyclone
Rashid.notes: Strike hitbox; spawns a tornado with 1 hit of projectile durability; cancelable into 4K Wing Stroke or 6K Rolling Assault on frames 21-22; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to both hits; high active frame count makes it great for oki; 28f recovery is total time after the tornado spawns; 14f recovery is total time after tornado disappears; advantage when canceled into 6K Roll: '''-5'''/'''-13'''

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; on block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); on hit, Rashid gets better KD Advantage on later active frames; opponent slides on the ground for great corner carry; can be affected by Air Current on frames 6-27

Rashid.name: Eagle Spike (Air Current)
Rashid.notes: Functions identically to enhanced 214HK; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; on hit/block, bounces off opponent with extra recovery (frame advantage unaffected by which active frame connects); opponent slides on the ground for great corner carry; Punish Counter tumble allows for a follow-up 214K for even more damage and corner carry

Rashid.name: Arabian Cyclone
Rashid.notes: Strike hitbox; spawns a tornado with 1 hit of projectile durability; cancelable into 4K Wing Stroke or 6K Rolling Assault on frames 26-27; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to both hits; high active frame count makes it great for oki; in the corner, Rashid can consistently link 5LK on hit; 26f recovery is total time after the tornado spawns; 12f recovery is total time after tornado disappears; safe against Drive Reversal if the opponent blocks the 2nd hit; advantage when canceled into 6K Roll: '''-5'''/'''-13'''

Rashid.name: Arabian Cyclone
Rashid.notes: Strike hitbox (making it vulnerable to opponent's wakeup SA1); spawns a tornado with 1 hit of OD projectile durability; first hit puts opponent into limited juggle state; the tornado does not cause a knockdown on its own; cancelable into 4K Wing Stroke or 6K Rolling Assault on frames 26-27; creates an Air Current on frame 53 (after the first tornado dissipates) that lasts 60f and enhances many of Rashid's moves; 4f extra recovery on block; the listed recovery time begins after the tornado's first active frame (Rashid recovers before the tornado disappears); advantage when canceled into 6K Roll: KD+39/'''-16'''

Rashid.name: Wing Stroke
Rashid.notes: Cancelable into air normals/specials on frames 32-51; can be affected by Air Current on frames 23-47; 6f landing recovery occurs if no air move is used

Rashid.name: Rolling Assault
Rashid.notes: Crouching state 6-33f; cancelable into Nail Assault follow-up on frames 17-20; can be affected by Air Current on frames 8-25; can roll under most projectiles (loses to low ones like Juri 236LK or Rashid 236KK); Hit/Block Advantage after 214P connects: 214LP/214MP '''-5/-13'''; 214HP KD+43/+1; 214PP KD+39/'''-16'''

Rashid.name: Nail Assault
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state; crouching state for entire move duration; cannot hit cross-ups behind Rashid; outside of juggles, only combos naturally from 214HP/214PP versions

Rashid.name: Super Rashid Kick
Rashid.notes: Useful anti-air and combo/juggle tool; deals 300 less damage vs. airborne opponents with variable KD Advantage based on juggle height; grounded hit gives a cinematic that switches sides; bounces far away on block, but easily punished with dash or Drive Rush starter; listed recovery is on whiff/(block); only 500 damage on first hit if it trades

Rashid.name: Altair
Rashid.notes: Reaches about half screen; cinematic time regenerates ~1.8 Drive bars for Rashid; only deals 10 damage when trading with opponent's attack

Rashid.name: Altair (CA)
Rashid.notes: Reaches about half screen; 1f better KD Advantage over non-CA version; available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Rashid; only deals 10 damage when trading with opponent's attack

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: Good anti-air that can hit cross-ups; can be affected by Air Current on frames 2-5; if the final hit whiffs as an anti-air, Rashid can get a follow-up juggle

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: Good anti-air that can hit cross-ups

Rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot
Rashid.notes: 1-hit projectile that travels forward before arcing upward; can hold button to charge for a powered-up version; trajectory depends on button strength (LK = farthest/horizontal, MK = middle, HK = shortest/vertical); projectile comes out in 6f if button is released from frames 11-27 (total startup 17-33f); cannot use if SA2 is active

Rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot
Rashid.notes: 2-hit OD projectile; 2nd hit puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; travels fullscreen; hitbox is low to the ground, making many low-profile anti-projectile moves ineffective; projectile comes out in 6f if button is released from frames 11-34 (total startup 17-40f); cannot use if SA2 is active

Rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot (Hold)
Rashid.notes: 3-hit OD projectile; 3rd hit puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; must hold button 32f for fully charged version; travels fullscreen; cancelable into Wing Stroke (4K) and Rolling Assault (6K) follow-ups on frame 55 (can be buffered on frame 37 onward); cancel into Roll is -4 oB from point blank but massively plus on block from farther away; hitbox is low to the ground, making many low-profile anti-projectile moves ineffective; creates Air Current effect on frame 38 next to Rashid that lasts 70f and enhances many of his moves; cannot use if SA2 is active

Rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot (Hold)
Rashid.notes: 3-hit projectile; trajectory depends on button strength (LK = farthest/horizontal, MK = middle, HK = shortest/vertical); must hold button 48f for fully charged version; counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to all hits; creates Air Current effect on frame 51 next to Rashid that lasts 60f and enhances many of his moves; cannot use if SA2 is active

Rashid.name: Whirlwind Shot (Partial Hold)
Rashid.notes: 2-hit projectile; trajectory depends on button strength (LK = farthest/horizontal, MK = middle, HK = shortest/vertical); must hold button 28f; counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to both hits; projectile comes out in 6f if button is released from frames 28-47 (total startup 34-53f); cannot use if SA2 is active

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: Great pressure tool that is safe on block and can blow throw armor; 5f extra recovery on whiff; Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies through all hits (allows for follow-up combo); can be affected by Air Current on frames 2-16; if the 3rd hit whiffs in a Burnout pressure sequence, Rashid is safe at -3 oB

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: Fullscreen advancing move that gives a combo on hit and frame advantage on block; counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies through all hits (allows for a stronger follow-up combo)

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: The last 11f of landing recovery is cancelable into special moves or supers on hit only; 4f worse advantage and 1 less hit when crouch blocked; cannot anti-air cross-ups; can be affected by Air Current on frames 2-8

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: On block, gets +1 hit vs. tall standing characters, and -1 hit vs. crouching characters (affects block data, chip, meter gain, etc.); cannot anti-air cross-ups; travels fullscreen

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: Shorter animation with less landing recovery on block only; cannot anti-air cross-ups; can only hit twice vs. grounded opponents (will not break DI armor); 5f extra knockdown advantage if the final hit whiffs (keeps Rashid safe); can be affected by Air Current on frames 2-8

Rashid.name: Spinning Mixer
Rashid.notes: Cannot anti-air cross-ups; 12f worse advantage and 2 fewer hits when crouch blocked; on hit or block, Rashid can cancel into j.214K on frames 67-71 after the active period

Rashid.name: Cyclone Slicer
Rashid.notes: Can be juggled into even without Drive Rush; 4f extra recovery on block; disadvantage on block is fixed regardless of which active frame connects (cannot make it safer when meaty)

Rashid.name: Crouching Heavy Punch
Rashid.notes: Decent poke that can be buffered into supers; good close range Punish Counter starter (combos into 5HP), but high pushback makes it less reliable at longer ranges; 2 extra recovery frames on whiff; topmost hurtboxes on frames 8-14 are projectile invincible (avoids Sagat's MP/HP Tiger Shot)

Rashid.name: Crouching Light Kick
Rashid.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK

Rashid.name: Crouching Light Punch
Rashid.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-7 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air)

Rashid.name: Crouching Medium Kick
Rashid.notes: Standard cancelable low poke; Range: 1.405; DR cancel is delayed until after active frames

Rashid.name: Crouching Medium Punch
Rashid.notes: Combo and pressure tool with many active frames for easy oki; can anti-air on frames 7-9 but cannot hit opponents behind Rashid; whiffs on crouching opponents at longer ranges unless they extend a vertical hurtbox

Rashid.name: Sunset Drop
Rashid.notes: Side switches; Rashid can pressure with DR~6HK (+1 oB) midscreen or corner; or DR~2HP in the corner (huge pushback, links to SA1); a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Rashid.name: Back Taunt
Rashid.notes: "Check this out! Now you try."

Rashid.name: Standing Heavy Kick
Rashid.notes: Puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; Punish Counter launches grounded opponents into limited juggle state and causes airborne opponents to fall closer to Rashid; decent anti-air hitbox, but very slow and cannot hit cross-up; high pushback on hit and block; forces stand on hit; final 2 active frames whiff on crouching opponents unless they extend a vertical hurtbox; has an extended hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles

Rashid.name: Standing Heavy Punch
Rashid.notes: Decent mid-range button with a strong hitbox for counterpoking; can combo to 214HK after Drive Rush or Punish Counter; special/DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame

Rashid.name: Standing Light Kick
Rashid.notes: Highest hitstun light normal makes it useful for special cancels (the only light normal that can combo into 214LK naturally); DR cancel is delayed until after active frames

Rashid.name: Standing Light Punch
Rashid.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK

Rashid.name: Standing Medium Kick
Rashid.notes: Combo starter that links into 5MP or into itself on counter-hit; 2 extra recovery frames on whiff

Rashid.name: Standing Medium Punch
Rashid.notes: Useful for starting combos and block pressure; has a Target Combo follow-up that can be canceled into 236LP for safety on block or into higher damage routes on hit

Rashid.name: Rising Kick
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state; both hits form a true blockstring and can cancel to 236LP for safety; special/DR cancel is delayed until after 4th recovery frame

Rashid.name: Neutral Taunt
Rashid.notes: "Do this... and this... and this. It's easy as pie."; hurtbox shifts as Rashid moves (lower body invuln frames 52-74, 83-107, 208-236; low profile 121-141, 169-186)

Rashid.name: Run
Rashid.notes: Input by holding forward after a forward dash; cancelable into 6P or 6K follow-ups on frames 18-72; after 72f, Rashid has 18f stopping recovery if no follow-up is input (90f total); stopping the run early has 5f recovery; no stopping recovery if jumping forward out of the run animation (neutral/back jump still plays out the 5f recovery); counter-hit state during entire run animation; affected by Air Current for entire duration except for 18f recovery, causing Rashid to run faster

Rashid.name: Tempest Moon
Rashid.notes: Counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to both hits; frames 1-3 can be affected by Air Current, becoming the Enhanced version

Rashid.name: Tempest Moon (Air Current)
Rashid.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle OTG state if first hit connects (regular knockdown if first hit doesn't connect)

Rashid.name: Backup
Rashid.notes: Crouching state for entire move duration; on hit, connects twice and switches sides, remaining projectile invincible throughout the entire animation; on block, connects once and stays on the same side; if opponent is cornered, Rashid is close enough for a follow-up combo; counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to both hits; frames 1-17 can be affected by Air Current

Rashid.name: Crescent Kick
Rashid.notes: 3f extra recovery on whiff; useful for hopping over low pokes and comboing into MP normals on Punish Counter, but not actually airborne; good option out of Drive Rush; can be spaced to hit on later active frames for better advantage; can be affected by Air Current on frames 6-19 (travels fullscreen)

Rashid.name: Beak Assault
Rashid.notes: Long-ranged overhead that can lead to combos if well-spaced; not actually airborne despite the animation; can be affected by Air Current on frames 4-25 (travels nearly fullscreen)

Rashid.name: Eagle Slash (Block)
Rashid.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; see [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Reversal|Drive Reversal]].

Rashid.name: Eagle Slash (Recovery)
Rashid.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze; see [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Reversal|Drive Reversal]].

Rashid.name: Side Flip
Rashid.notes: Can input 4KK/5KK/6KK follow-up on frames 19-25; collision box disappears frames 8-23, allowing Rashid to pass through opponents; can be affected by Air Current on frames 2-20, traveling nearly fullscreen; travel distance: 1.7 (3.62 enhanced)

Rashid.name: Front Flip
Rashid.notes: Input during 6KK; holding forward/back/neutral direction affects flip distance; can use any air attack frames 22-40; can be affected by Air Current on frames 1-36, traveling forward fullscreen

Rashid.name: Flapping Spin
Rashid.notes: () refers to startup of 2nd hit; 1st hit puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state (or maintains juggle state when used mid-combo); 2nd hit causes air reset; counter-hit/Punish Counter bonus advantage applies to both hits; decent range for whiff punishing; can be affected by Air Current on frames 3-10 (travels fullscreen)

Rashid.name: Forward Taunt
Rashid.notes: "Hmm? Hey look, just relax and have fun, alright?"

Rashid.name: Eagle Edge
Rashid.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Impact|Drive Impact]]. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

Rashid.name: Arabian Skyhigh
Rashid.notes: From forward jump or 6KK~KK only; 1st active frame can only connect in juggles; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; has minimum height restriction (will not activate after low-height j.2HP); KD Advantage varies greatly based on the height it connects; performs a double-jump after the initial flip kick (longest trajectory); can be affected by Air Current on frames 1-21

Rashid.name: Arabian Skyhigh
Rashid.notes: From forward jump or 6KK~KK only; 1st active frame can only connect in juggles; puts opponent into limited juggle OTG state on hit; has minimum height restriction (will not activate after low-height j.2HP); performs a double-jump after the initial flip kick; on hit, transitions into a follow-up divekick that is projectile invincible; can be affected by Air Current on frames 1-13

Rashid.name: Arabian Skyhigh
Rashid.notes: From forward jump or 6KK~KK only; 1st active frame can only connect in juggles; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; has minimum height restriction (will not activate after low-height j.2HP); KD Advantage varies greatly based on the height it connects; performs a double-jump after the initial flip kick (shortest trajectory); can be affected by Air Current on frames 1-13

Rashid.name: Arabian Skyhigh
Rashid.notes: From forward jump or 6KK~KK only; 1st active frame can only connect in juggles; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; has minimum height restriction (will not activate after low-height j.2HP); KD Advantage varies greatly based on the height it connects; performs a double-jump after the initial flip kick (medium trajectory, similar to normal jump); can be affected by Air Current on frames 1-18

Rashid.name: Blitz Strike
Rashid.notes: Can be performed during forward jump or after j.214K; causes spike knockdown and OTG juggle state vs. airborne opponents; cancelable into j.214K; bounces off opponent on hit/block/parry, allowing Rashid to follow up with another airborne move (except another j.2HP) on frames 12-23; if Rashid hits airborne opponent 1f before landing, he lands immediately rather than bouncing; listed frame advantage assumes a grounded opponent and no follow-up air attack; juggle data in () refers to version after j.214K; lower body projectile invuln 10-19f except around attack hitbox

Rashid.name: Aerial Shot
Rashid.notes: During neutral jump only; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state, making it a useful air-to-air; lower body projectile invuln 8-19f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Rashid.name: Jumping Heavy Kick
Rashid.notes: When used after j.214K or 214P~4K, causes a spike knockdown vs. airborne opponents; lower body projectile invuln 10-19f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Rashid.name: Jumping Heavy Punch
Rashid.notes: 1st hit puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state, 2nd hit causes spike knockdown; if 1st hit is stand blocked, the 2nd hit will not hit overhead against crouch block; lower body projectile invuln 8-23f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Rashid.name: Jumping Light Kick
Rashid.notes: Longest horizontal range of Rashid's jump normals

Rashid.name: Jumping Light Punch
Rashid.notes: Quick air-to-air

Rashid.name: Desert Slider
Rashid.notes: Useful air-to-air against close range jumps; in the corner, can get oki with Drive Rush

Rashid.name: Jumping Medium Kick
Rashid.notes: Cross-up; lower body projectile invuln 7-20f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Rashid.name: Jumping Medium Punch
Rashid.notes: Puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; cancels into j.214K from forward jumps; lower body projectile invuln 9-22f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Rashid.name: Riding Glider
Rashid.notes: Allows for a corner throw loop by holding Run for 18-20f, then letting go before throwing (17-20f for Blanka/E.Honda/Zangief); a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Rashid.name: Drive Parry
Rashid.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Parry|Drive Parry]]. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

Rashid.name: Drive Rush Cancel
Rashid.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Rush|Drive Rush]]; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

Rashid.name: Parry Drive Rush
Rashid.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Rush|Drive Rush]]; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.796 (min/throw), 2.253 (min/block), 2.998 (max/final DR frame)

Rashid.name: Wall Jump
Rashid.notes: Counter-hit state during entire duration; can be done from Back or Neutral jump if fully against the wall, or after Forward Jump against a cornered opponent; cannot be performed after j.2HP or j.214K

Ryu.name: Shin Hashogeki Lv.1
Ryu.notes: Can hold the button to charge to a higher level for more damage (in exchange for less invincibility); if button is held up to 5f after Super freeze, this invuln is extended up to the 2nd active frame (up to 18f); strike hitbox; Burnout chip damage does not changed based on charge level

Ryu.name: Denjin Hashogeki Lv.1
Ryu.notes: Can hold the button to charge to a higher level for more damage (in exchange for less invincibility); if button is held up to 5f after Super freeze, this invuln is extended up to the 2nd active frame (up to 18f); strike hitbox; Burnout chip damage does not changed based on charge level; consumes Denjin stock for slightly more damage

Ryu.name: Denjin Hashogeki Lv.2
Ryu.notes: Loses 4 invincibility frames if held; invincibility can be reduced to 1-7f if the button is held the minimum length of time for Lv.2 charge (6f after Super freeze); strike hitbox; Burnout chip damage does not changed based on charge level; consumes Denjin stock for slightly more damage; Denjin version gives the tumbling OTG state that can lead to follow-up juggles (this is the only version that incurs damage scaling in combos)

Ryu.name: Denjin Hashogeki Lv.3
Ryu.notes: Loses 4 invincibility frames if held; full charge causes tumble OTG state; strike hitbox; Burnout chip damage does not changed based on charge level; extremely high pushback on block (can be difficult to punish without holding Parry into immediate Drive Rush); consumes Denjin stock for slightly more damage

Ryu.name: Shin Hashogeki Lv.2
Ryu.notes: Loses 4 invincibility frames if held; invincibility can be reduced to 1-7f if the button is held the minimum length of time for Lv.2 charge (6f after Super freeze); strike hitbox; Burnout chip damage does not changed based on charge level

Ryu.name: Shin Hashogeki Lv.3
Ryu.notes: Loses 4 invincibility frames if held; full charge causes tumble OTG state; strike hitbox; Burnout chip damage does not changed based on charge level; extremely high pushback on block (can be difficult to punish without holding Parry into immediate Drive Rush)

Ryu.name: Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Only 1st hit can connect on crouching (stand blocking any hit forces next hit to be blocked, even if crouching); later hits have better KD Advantage; puts opponent into limited juggle state (can juggle afterward if 3rd hit connects)

Ryu.name: Hashogeki
Ryu.notes: 2 hits, even if it connects on final active frame; strike hitbox but can nullify 1-hit meterless projectiles; puts opponent into spinning juggle state on hit; leaves Ryu inside throw range for a strike/throw mixup on block

Ryu.name: Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Can hit crouching opponents; puts opponent into limited juggle state; on hit, 1st hit has vacuum effect; on max range block, some hits can drop (-32 at worse)

Ryu.name: Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Can hit crouching opponents

Ryu.name: Hashogeki
Ryu.notes: Strike hitbox but can nullify 1-hit meterless projectiles; puts opponent into spinning juggle state on counter-hit/Punish Counter; excellent Burnout pressure tool (+1 on block, but increased pushback against Burnout)

Ryu.name: Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Only 1st hit can connect on crouching (stand blocking 1st hit forces 2nd hit to be blocked, even if crouching); later hits have better KD Advantage

Ryu.name: Hashogeki
Ryu.notes: Strike hitbox but can nullify 1-hit meterless projectiles; puts opponent into spinning juggle state on counter-hit/Punish Counter

Ryu.name: Denjin Charge Hashogeki
Ryu.notes: () refers to recovery on block; strike hitbox but can nullify 2-hit meterless projectile; puts opponent into spinning juggle state on hit; only comes out when the Heavy Punch button is pressed

Ryu.name: Hashogeki
Ryu.notes: Strike hitbox but can nullify 1-hit OD projectiles or any meterless projectiles; great pressure tool

Ryu.name: Denjin Charge Hashogeki
Ryu.notes: 1-hit; strike hitbox but can nullify 1-hit OD projectile or any meterless projectile; crumple state is +14 before opponent becomes airborne

Ryu.name: Denjin Charge
Ryu.notes: Charges up next fireball-based move (Hadoken, Hashogeki, SA1, SA2) into a more powerful Denjin version; Ryu is in a counter-hit state for the entire animation; gains the Denjin charge on frame 50; can only store 1 stock at a time (does not persist between rounds); can also be performed after 5HP~HK or 5MP~LK~HK (on hit) by inputting 2P

Ryu.name: Shin Shoryuken
Ryu.notes: More hits connect on block vs. tall standing characters (these extra hits do not deal any additional Drive Damage on block); active frames 3-12 cause a non-cinematic hit that does reduced damage (400x4,2000); cannot anti-air cross-ups; starts up faster only when canceled from HP Shoryuken; cinematic time regenerates ~2.2 Drive bars for Ryu

Ryu.name: Shin Shoryuken (CA)
Ryu.notes: More hits connect on block vs. tall standing characters (these extra hits do not deal any additional Drive Damage on block); active frames 3-12 cause a non-cinematic hit that does slightly reduced damage (400x2,1200x3); cannot anti-air cross-ups; starts up faster only when canceled from HP Shoryuken; available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~2.3 Drive bars for Ryu

Ryu.name: Shinku Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 5-hit Super projectile; button strength does not affect projectile speed; opponent cannot jump over projectile after Super freeze if within ~1/2 screen; can be preformed even when an OD Hadoken is on screen

Ryu.name: Denjin Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 8-hit Super projectile; button strength does not affect projectile speed; opponent cannot jump over projectile after Super freeze if within ~1/2 screen; consumes Denjin stock for slightly more damage and KD Advantage; can be performed even when an OD Hadoken is on screen

Ryu.name: High Blade Kick
Ryu.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit (can follow up with 623MP, 623PP, or SA3 in corner); Punish Counter tumble state can be hit OTG; has great range and forward movement, making it a useful poke in neutral; the last 3 active frames have identical range (the listed best-case frame advantage is when spaced at max range, active frame 7)

Ryu.name: Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 1-hit projectile; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state

Ryu.name: High Blade Kick
Ryu.notes: Wall Bounce into limited juggle state on hit; if close to corner, opponent flies over Ryu's head

Ryu.name: High Blade Kick
Ryu.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; sets up auto-timed safe jump against cornered opponents; can combo when canceled from any normal except 5LP; the last 2 active frames have identical range (the listed best-case frame advantage is when spaced at max range, active frame 5)

Ryu.name: Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 1-hit projectile; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state

Ryu.name: High Blade Kick
Ryu.notes: Puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; can be spaced safely due to its range and high active frame count; 3 extra recovery frames on whiff; the last 3 active frames have identical range (the listed best-case frame advantage is when spaced at max range, active frame 7)

Ryu.name: Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 1-hit projectile; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state

Ryu.name: Denjin Charge Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 2-hit projectile; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit; only comes out when the HP button is pressed

Ryu.name: Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 2-hit OD projectile; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit

Ryu.name: Denjin Charge Hadoken
Ryu.notes: 3-hit OD projectile; puts opponent into limited juggle state on hit

Ryu.name: Low Spinning Sweep
Ryu.notes: Good range and hitbox priority; has some juggle potential; on block, always plays out a fixed 29f recovery (cannot be made safer with meaty timing)

Ryu.name: Crouching Heavy Punch
Ryu.notes: Forces stand on hit; decent anti-air; cannot hit cross-ups; fist hurtbox is invincible to air strikes on frame 9; head hurtbox is invincible to air strikes on frames 10-14; only 1st active frame is cancelable (extends a combo-only hitbox to match the range of the 2nd active frame for combo consistency); () refers to hit/block recovery on 1st active frame only; 5f less hitstun on active frames 2-5 (can be punishable on meaty timing)

Ryu.name: Crouching Light Kick
Ryu.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK

Ryu.name: Crouching Light Punch
Ryu.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-5 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air)

Ryu.name: Crouching Medium Kick
Ryu.notes: Range: 1.482; DR cancel is delayed until after active frames

Ryu.name: Crouching Medium Punch
Ryu.notes: 2f extra recovery on whiff; combo and pressure tool; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-9 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air); extends a wider hurtbox until the end of recovery

Ryu.name: Down Taunt
Ryu.notes: "Come!"

Ryu.name: Axe Kick
Ryu.notes: () refers to 2nd hit startup; 1st hit forces stand and puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; 2nd hit puts airborne opponents into OTG bounce state; both hits are cancelable; Counter-hit and Punish Counter frame advantage applies to both hits

Ryu.name: Short Uppercut
Ryu.notes: Forces stand on hit; only 1st active frame is cancelable; () refers to hit/block recovery on 1st active frame only; extremely short range makes it finicky in combos; 8f less hitstun on active frames 2-4 (can be punishable with meaty timing)

Ryu.name: Somersault Throw
Ryu.notes: Side switches; no throw/strike oki after back throwing opponent into corner; a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Ryu.name: Back Taunt
Ryu.notes: "Your footwork's sloppy."

Ryu.name: Standing Heavy Kick
Ryu.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend a vertical hurtbox; 2 extra recovery frames on block; good horizontal anti-air that puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state (higher launch on Punish Counter juggle); '''+11''' before Punish Counter crumple state goes airborne; extends a hurtbox 1f before active that is vulnerable to projectiles

Ryu.name: Standing Heavy Punch
Ryu.notes: Forces stand on hit (allowing Target Combo follow-up to work on crouching opponents); good poke with hitbox priority, many active frames, and a reactable hitconfirm window

Ryu.name: High Double Strike
Ryu.notes: HK cannot hit vs. crouch block (much more unsafe); cancels to Denjin Charge by inputting 2P on hit only (KD Adv. +10); can juggle into MP/OD Shoryuken or SA3 in the corner

Ryu.name: Standing Light Kick
Ryu.notes: Good range for a 5f light (useful in punishes and neutral buffers); DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd active frame

Ryu.name: Standing Light Punch
Ryu.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK

Ryu.name: Standing Medium Kick
Ryu.notes: Solid poke; front leg hurtbox is raised on frames 4-11 (can avoid low pokes)

Ryu.name: Standing Medium Punch
Ryu.notes: 2f extra recovery on whiff; useful combo tool with a Target Combo follow-up; extends a wider body hurtbox until the end of recovery

Ryu.name: Fuwa Triple Strike 1
Ryu.notes: Hits consistently at max 5MP range, but the LK can whiff if 5MP connects on an extended hurtbox; can be spaced safely against most characters for a spacing trap

Ryu.name: Fuwa Triple Strike 2
Ryu.notes: (refers to scaled damage); 6f gap before HK on block; cancels to Denjin Charge by inputting 2P on hit only (KD Adv. +7)

Ryu.name: Neutral Taunt
Ryu.notes: "Come on!"

Ryu.name: Shoryuken
Ryu.notes: Has juggle potential; cannot hit cross-up; does reduced damage and higher juggle limit on active frames 3-10 (weaker as a high-connect anti-air); higher knockdown advantage on the first 2 active frames (+37 refers to 1st active frame, +29 refers to anti-air with 3rd active frame; actual advantage varies based on height/distance)

Ryu.name: Shoryuken
Ryu.notes: Has juggle potential; puts opponent into limited juggle state (can juggle after a high corner anti-air); cannot hit cross-up; does reduced damage and higher juggle limit on active frames 4-10 (weaker as a high-connect anti-air)

Ryu.name: Shoryuken
Ryu.notes: Has juggle potential; cannot hit cross-up; does reduced damage and higher juggle limit on active frames 4-10 (weaker as a high-connect anti-air)

Ryu.name: Shoryuken
Ryu.notes: Has juggle potential; cannot hit cross-up; only 2nd hit will connect if used too early as an anti-air; extends a combo-only hitbox to make the 1st active frame more consistent

Ryu.name: Whirlwind Kick
Ryu.notes: Cancelable to regular/OD Air Tatsu on hit/block; Low Crush on frames 13-20 (not airborne); high pushback on block; puts airborne opponents into limited juggle state; good juggle option after midscreen OD High Blade Kick for corner carry and oki; proximity guard box begins on frame 2 and reaches the maximum attack range (prevents opponents from walking back out of the attack startup)

Ryu.name: Aerial Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Version canceled from 6HK; no follow-up juggle like after jumping Air Tatsu; the last frame of recovery puts Ryu in a crouching state; useful juggle ender after midscreen OD High Blade Kick for damage, corner carry, and oki

Ryu.name: Aerial Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Version canceled from 6HK; can hit crouching opponents unlike the jumping version; puts opponent into limited juggle state (follow-up only possible near the corner); the last frame of recovery puts Ryu in a crouching state

Ryu.name: Solar Plexus Strike
Ryu.notes: 2 hits; good forward-moving combo starter and pressure tool; if 1st hit connects on an extended hurtbox, becomes '''+6''' on Counter-hit or '''+8''' on Punish Counter; Counter-hit/Punish Counter frame advantage applies to both hits; can be very advantageous if 1st hit trades with a light normal; 1st hit puts opponent into free juggle state so that the 2nd hit connects (to prevent Ryu from being punishable)

Ryu.name: Chest Strike (Block)
Ryu.notes: Performed by inputting 6HPHK during blockstun; 5f extra recovery on hit; freezes the screen for 4f during startup; see [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Reversal|Drive Reversal]].

Ryu.name: Chest Strike (Recovery)
Ryu.notes: Performed by holding 6HPHK on wakeup; 5f extra recovery on hit; does not have any screen freeze; see [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Reversal|Drive Reversal]].

Ryu.name: Collarbone Breaker
Ryu.notes: Counter-hit/Punish Counter/Drive Rush frame advantage applies to both hits; 2nd hit is no longer an overhead if the first hit connects; up to +5 on hit with meaty timing for a meterless combo extension

Ryu.name: Forward Taunt
Ryu.notes: *Slaps face*

Ryu.name: Shingeki
Ryu.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Impact|Drive Impact]]. Airborne connect gives spinning juggle state on Punish Counter or corner Wall Splat with variable height.

Ryu.name: Aerial Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Can be input during forward jump; not an overhead; can cross-up (4f less blockstun when landing as a cross-up); at least +3 on block vs. crouching opponents; puts opponent into limited juggle state (can juggle 2HK or SA1); the last 13f of recovery puts Ryu in a crouching state

Ryu.name: Aerial Tatsumaki Senpu-kyaku
Ryu.notes: Can be input during forward jump; cannot hit cross-up; cannot hit crouching opponents (unless they extend a vertical hurtbox), and 1st hit can only hit standing opponents on the final 3 airborne frames of jump; puts opponent into limited juggle state; the last 13f of recovery puts Ryu in a crouching state

Ryu.name: Jumping Heavy Kick
Ryu.notes: Strong jump-in from mid to long range; lower body projectile invuln 10-17f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Ryu.name: Jumping Heavy Punch
Ryu.notes: Spike knockdown on counter hit/Punish Counter vs. airborne opponents; lower body projectile invuln 9-23f except around attack hitbox (cannot be used to avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Ryu.name: Jumping Light Kick
Ryu.notes: Cross-up

Ryu.name: Jumping Light Punch
Ryu.notes: Can be used as a fuzzy instant overhead

Ryu.name: Jumping Medium Kick
Ryu.notes: Cross-up; lower body projectile invuln 7-20f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Ryu.name: Jumping Medium Punch
Ryu.notes: Both hits are cancelable to Air Tatsu and put airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; if 1st hit is stand blocked, the 2nd hit will not hit overhead against crouch block; lower body projectile invuln 8-22f (if used immediately on the way up, can avoid the 2nd hit of JP's OD Amnesia bombs)

Ryu.name: Shoulder Throw
Ryu.notes: Has access to corner throw loops without walking or dashing (whiff 5LP or manually time the next throw); a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Ryu.name: Drive Parry
Ryu.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Parry|Drive Parry]]. Perfect Parrying has only 1F of recovery and disables the opponent from canceling their attack. Perfect Parrying projectiles puts you into fixed 11 frames of recovery. After a Perfect Parry, all Super Gauge gain is reduced by 20% and Drive Gauge gain/damage is reduced by 50% for the entire punish combo.

Ryu.name: Drive Rush Cancel
Ryu.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Rush|Drive Rush]]; 3-bar version performed on hit/block from a cancelable normal; can also be performed on whiff from cancelable light normals; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation; the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties

Ryu.name: Parry Drive Rush
Ryu.notes: See [[Street_Fighter_6/Gauges#Drive_Rush|Drive Rush]]; 1-bar version performed out of a Parry; startup refers to minimum time before an attack can cancel the Drive Rush animation (if performed immediately after a successful Parry, only 1+8 startup); the first 15 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack; the final 22 recovery frames are cancelable into any attack or movement option or blocking (except Parry); only Normal and Command Normal attacks are enhanced with +4 frame advantage and improved juggle properties; Distance: 0.525 (min/throw), 1.878 (min/block), 3.628 (max/final DR frame)

Sagat.name: Savage Tiger
Sagat.notes: Goes into one of 4 follow-ups after frame 76 on hit (depending on which direction is held while clutching the opponent); Sagat's best reversal Super (but is still slow enough to be baited by an opponent's safejab setup); can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; Sagat has travel time throughout the active frames (takes longer than SA3 to reach full range)

Sagat.name:
Savage Tiger Stomp
(Oki)
Sagat.notes: Leaves the opponent close to Sagat for stronger oki than other versions; can walk up for a strike/throw/shimmy mixup; gives enough advantage for an immediate 6MP overhead

Sagat.name:
Savage Tiger Pendulum
(Side Switch)
Sagat.notes: Switches sides with opponent; leaves the opponent far away with no oki

Sagat.name:
Savage Tiger Raid
(Damage)
Sagat.notes: Highest damage variant of SA2; leaves the opponent far away with no oki; has significant corner carry (over 1/2 screen)

Sagat.name:
Savage Tiger Zenith
(Launcher)
Sagat.notes: Launches the opponent into a limited juggle state (juggle counter is always set to 2 regardless of previous juggle state); Hard Knockdown if the opponent hits the ground instead of being juggled; useful for corner carry, building back some Super gauge, and getting a good mix of damage + oki (but usually results in less damage than Tiger Raid)

Sagat.name: Tiger Nexus
Sagat.notes: Slow startup, only combos naturally from the first hit of 5HK (requires Drive Rush or Punish Counter to combo from 2HP, 4HP launch, or 5HK 2nd hit); 214HK cannot frame trap when canceled from a normal (except for Burnout + Drive Rush into 2MP/2HP/5HK); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; can juggle after DR~4HP (easier execution but less damaging than his MP Tiger Shot juggle sequence); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214HK)

Sagat.name: Tiger Nexus
Sagat.notes: Similar to HK version but faster (can cancel from more starters like 2HP, 4HP launch, and 5HK 2nd hit); combos naturally into all follow-ups including 6HK; cancel into 6HK follow-up leaves a 7f gap on block (can frame trap 4f normals in Burnout); 2f extra recovery on Perfect Parry only; if the 1st hit is Perfect Parried, 2nd hit will interrupt any punish slower than 5f startup (trades with 6f attacks); cannot perform follow-up attacks if both hits whiff; carries Counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214KK)

Sagat.name: Nova Tiger
Sagat.notes: Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; combos naturally from 214KK; after blocked 214KK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214KK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

Sagat.name: Mighty Tiger
Sagat.notes: Mixup tool that is unsafe on block; the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; safe vs. Burnout but no longer frame traps, making it a weak option; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (e.g. after DI wallsplat juggle); causes immediate knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK unless the 6LK input is delayed

Sagat.name: Greedy Tiger
Sagat.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (only allows 623LP/PP juggle in the corner); frame data vs. crouch from 214KK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC; safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214KK; 3f blockstring gap after 214KK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

Sagat.name: Nova Tiger
Sagat.notes: Connects on both standing/crouching opponents; launches opponent into a limited juggle state; only combos naturally from 214HK (requires juggle state for LK/MK versions, like a CH/PC Tiger Nexus); after blocked 214LK/MK, interruptible 9f blockstring gap (5f gap vs. Burnout, loses to 4f normals); after blocked 214HK, interruptible 7f blockstring gap (frame trap vs. Burnout); unsafe to reversal Drive Impact and susceptible to Perfect Parry on reaction (becomes DI-safe from 214HK if opponent delays it by 2f or longer); opponent is left inside throw range on block (but Sagat cannot shimmy an immediate throw tech)

Sagat.name: Mighty Tiger
Sagat.notes: Mixup tool that is unsafe on block; the threat of overhead makes ~6MK follow-up stronger while the threat of a frame trap makes ~6HK follow-up stronger; safe vs. Burnout but no longer frame traps (unless the 6LK input is delayed from 214LK/MK); puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (e.g. after Counter-hit 214LK/MK); causes immediate knockdown on Counter-hit/Punish Counter; loses to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214LK/MK (but safe after 214HK unless the 6LK input is delayed); if used from a 2-light chain, opponent is in range for Throw or 2LK~5LP chain (too far if starting with 3-light chain)

Sagat.name: Greedy Tiger
Sagat.notes: Whiffs on crouching opponents; 2f extra recovery on whiff; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (only allows 623LP/PP juggle in the corner, or 623MP from CH/PC 214LK/MK launch); frame data vs. crouch from 214LK/214MK: -19 oH / -26 oB / KD +51 onPC launch; frame data vs. crouch from 214HK: -17 oH / -24 oB / -13 onPC (214HK keeps opponent crouching on Punish Counter); safe to reversal Drive Impact after blocked 214K; 5f blockstring gap after 214LK/MK (loses to reversal standing/crouching 4f normals); 3f blockstring gap after 214HK (frame trap vs. standing normals but still loses to reversal crouching normals); risky to attempt on block, but the threat of the overhead and frame trap from ~6LK follow-up can condition opponents to stand block or parry; opponent cannot walk back out of throw range on block

Sagat.name: Tiger Nexus
Sagat.notes: The only strength of 214K that can combo naturally from 5LP (3-light confirm can reach if point blank, but results in weaker mixup from ~6LK ender); does not frame trap when canceled on block (except from Light normals with Drive Rush or Burnout); combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214LK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214LK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

Sagat.name: Tiger Nexus
Sagat.notes: Combos into 6LK/6MK follow-ups; canceling into the 6HK follow-up leaves a 2f gap on hit / 9f gap on block (loses to 4f normals even in Burnout); Counter-hit/Punish Counter puts the opponent into a limited juggle state that allows the 6HK follow-up to combo; 214MK combos from canceled 2MP/2HP/5HK (these cancels also frame trap on block, with 2HP/5HK > 214MK being DI-safe); cannot perform follow-up attacks on whiff; lacks natural juggle potential but can juggle after DR~4HP (free juggle state) for a powerful 1-bar corner combo (DR~4HP > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP); opponents can beat all follow-ups with invincible reversals (but standard 6f reversals will not punish 214MK); if the opponent attempts to punish 214MK, the 6LK follow-up will frame trap on block (must delay 6LK vs. Burnout)

Sagat.name: Tiger Vanquisher
Sagat.notes: Cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

Sagat.name: Tiger Vanquisher (CA)
Sagat.notes: Available at 25% HP or below; cinematic time regenerates ~1.9 Drive bars for Sagat; only 2f startup when canceled from Tiger Uppercut; can be used as a projectile counter from about half screen; slow startup makes it a risky wakeup reversal option; total damage scaling from anti-air Tiger Uppercut is 20-40% depending on which strength was used (weaker strength gives higher scaling)

Sagat.name: Tiger Cannon
Sagat.notes: 8-hit Super projectile; can be used while OD Tiger Shot is on-screen (but not meterless Tiger Shot); fast travel speed allows it to be used in long range juggles; projectile speed is not affected by button strength

Sagat.name: Tiger Knee Crush
Sagat.notes: Furthest horizontal distance; much better block advantage when spaced at max range; 2nd hit active frames 1-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first hit whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+4 on block); if the 1st hit is crouch blocked, opponent cannot switch to stand block the 2nd hit; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 6 active frames connect, or 623MP / SA2 if the final active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; Sweet Spot occurs when juggling into the 3rd or 4th active frame, dealing 1300 damage (single hit) with a higher spinning juggle launch (ensures a follow-up juggle is possible even midscreen); the 2nd hit's extended Knee hitbox is too high to connect on standing characters on active frames 2-7 (tall characters: active frames 4-6); sets up corner safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

Sagat.name: High Tiger Shot
Sagat.notes: Fast 1-hit projectile; whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend an upward hurtbox; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; has much better recovery and frame advantage than the Low version; can be used meaty on the opponent's wakeup even if they crouch block, but the opponent can input a crouching button to avoid blocking the projectile; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 14-28 and a leg hurtbox on frames 14-42

Sagat.name: Tiger Knee Crush
Sagat.notes: 1st hit transitions to a different follow-up on hit, resulting in higher damage and a tumbling +66 knockdown (allows a 623LP juggle in the corner); if 1st hit whiffs, the next 2 hits deal 500 damage each and give a worse knockdown (only 1 hit at farthest ranges); safe on block but usually lands inside the opponent's throw range; 2nd hit active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out, it connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+1 on block); unlike HK Knee, the opponent can switch to stand block after the first hit connects, leaving Sagat at -2; blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; later hits put opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP)

Sagat.name: Tiger Knee Crush
Sagat.notes: Shortest horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 10-12 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +2) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-10 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it always connects on the last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last active frame connects); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents

Sagat.name: Low Tiger Shot
Sagat.notes: Fast 1-hit projectile (speed is not variable); can hit crouching opponents unlike MP/HP High Tiger Shot; has extremely long recovery compared to most projectiles (more vulnerable to jumps, Drive Impact, projectile invuln moves, and Perfect Parry + Drive Rush); the projectile travels low to the ground, preventing many low profile attacks from avoiding it (e.g. Kimberly's slide, A.K.I.'s Sinister Slide); Sagat is in a crouching state for the entire move duration with crouch-sized hurtboxes; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 16-43 and a leg hurtbox on frames 14-50; topmost hurtboxes are vulnerable only to air attacks on frames 1-50 (more vulnerable to jump-ins despite crouching) and are projectile invincible on frames 1-31 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 32-50 are still vulnerable)

Sagat.name: Low Tiger Shot
Sagat.notes: Fast 2-hit OD projectile; can hit crouching opponents; can be used while a meterless Tiger Shot is still on-screen; the projectile travels low to the ground, preventing many low profile attacks from avoiding it (e.g. Kimberly's slide, A.K.I.'s Sinister Slide); Sagat is in a crouching state for the entire move duration with crouch-sized hurtboxes; puts opponents into a limited juggle state; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 16-37 and a leg hurtbox on frames 12-44; topmost hurtboxes are vulnerable only to air attacks on frames 1-44 (more vulnerable to jump-ins despite crouching) and are projectile invincible on frames 1-29 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 30-44 are still vulnerable); starter scaling does not apply if only the 2nd hit connects (e.g. clashing with 1-hit OD fireball or breaking Drive Impact armor)

Sagat.name: Tiger Knee Crush
Sagat.notes: Medium horizontal distance; no front leg hurtbox on frames 14-15 (helps avoid low pokes); 3f extra landing recovery when absorbed by armor; much better block advantage (up to +3) when spaced at max range; active frames 2-9 whiff on crouching opponents; this means that if the Knee is spaced out so the first active frame whiffs, it connects on the 2nd to last active frame vs. crouching opponents (+2 on block, 623LP juggle on hit); puts opponent into a limited juggle state (in the corner, can juggle 623LP if the last 4 active frames connect); blocked Knee causes a screen shake when Sagat has frame advantage; can be whiffed in some situations for a side switch vs. knocked down opponents; sets up midscreen safe jump in certain juggle scenarios (e.g. after juggled 2MP~HP)

Sagat.name: High Tiger Shot
Sagat.notes: Medium speed 1-hit projectile (comparable to a shoto HP fireball, but much slower than Sagat's other projectiles); whiffs on crouching opponents unless they extend an upward hurtbox; puts airborne opponents into a limited juggle state (useful juggle tool after 4HP launch); has much better recovery and frame advantage than the Low version; can be used meaty on the opponent's wakeup even if they crouch block, but the opponent can input a crouching button to avoid blocking the projectile; extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 18-32 and a leg hurtbox on frames 18-42

Sagat.name: High Tiger Shot
Sagat.notes: Extremely fast 3-hit OD projectile; slow startup but very powerful in fireball wars once released; can hit crouching opponents unlike the MP/HP High Tiger Shots; can be used while a meterless Tiger Shot is still on-screen; excellent frame advantage on hit or block; puts opponents into a limited juggle state; can juggle into SA1 from anywhere on the screen, and into another OD High Tiger Shot from fullscreen (or at close range vs. cornered opponents); extends a slight projectile invincible arm hurtbox on frames 25-41 and a leg hurtbox on frames 25-48; starter scaling does not apply if only the 3rd hit connects (e.g. clashing with 2-hit OD fireball or breaking Drive Impact armor)

Sagat.name: Tiger Kick
Sagat.notes: Has some juggle potential; great range and hitbox priority; can be punished on block by most other sweeps in the game

Sagat.name: Crouching Heavy Punch
Sagat.notes: Very long range for a cancelable and hitconfirmable poke; significantly more range on active frames 3-4; topmost hurtbox is vulnerable only to aerial strikes on frames 1-14 (preventing its use as an anti-air), and is projectile invincible on frames 1-19 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 20-35 are still vulnerable)

Sagat.name: Crouching Light Kick
Sagat.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; low starter that can combo into any 3-light chain from close range

Sagat.name: Crouching Light Punch
Sagat.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; excellent range for a 4f jab; high pushback makes tick throw and counter-hit pressure weaker, but also allows Sagat to space himself outside the opponent's reversal normals on block; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd~3rd recovery frame; topmost hurtbox on frames 1-5 is vulnerable only to aerial strikes (preventing its use as an anti-air)

Sagat.name: Crouching Medium Kick
Sagat.notes: Amazing hitbox priority as a neutral poke; can link to 5LP at closer ranges, or into 2MP/5LK on Counter-hit; useful combo/pressure starter out of Drive Rush (but has poor link options near its max range)

Sagat.name: Crouching Medium Punch
Sagat.notes: Solid mid-range cancelable poke and buffer tool; 1f extra recovery on block; 3f extra recovery on whiff; significantly more range on active frames 2-3 (more effective linking from +8 or punishing -8 moves); cancelable into 2 different Target Combo follow-ups with different hitconfirm timings (requires Punish Counter or Drive Rush for 2MP~HP combo); topmost hurtbox is vulnerable only to aerial strikes on frames 1-9 (preventing its use as an anti-air), and is projectile invincible on frames 1-14 to avoid High Tiger Shot (frames 15-26 are still vulnerable)

Sagat.name: Tiger Rise
Sagat.notes: 3f blockstring gap between hits; harder to confirm into from 2MP but combos naturally; launch only allows a canceled Super but no other follow-up juggles; easily hitconfirmed into Super even if only the 2nd hit connects as a frame trap; higher KD advantage when juggled into

Sagat.name: Tiger Slash
Sagat.notes: Combos after Punish Counter or Drive Rush 2MP only; causes limited juggle OTG bounce vs. airborne opponents

Sagat.name: Tiger Monolith
Sagat.notes: Tall hitbox on 2nd hit, but also extends a tall hurtbox with no anti-air invincibility (likely to lose/trade with jump-ins); cannot hit cross-up; 2nd hit whiffs on crouch blocking opponents (3f worse on block and not cancelable); cancel does not occur until the 2nd hit's active frames (still executes on hit even if the 2nd hit whiffs); puts opponents into a limited juggle state (can combo into 236MP, DR~delay 4HP > 236HK, 623MP for great midscreen damage and corner carry); free juggle state from DR~4HP, allowing a more optimal corner juggle: > 214MK, 4HP > 236HK, 623MP; launches higher on Counter-hit/Punish Counter (KD +41) or on airborne opponents (KD +40); 1st hit puts opponent into a free juggle OTG bounce state that is usually overwritten by the 2nd hit (but can still occur on trades or when hitting extended hurtboxes)

Sagat.name: Tiger Carry
Sagat.notes: Side switch; no true oki after throwing opponent into the corner, but can pressure with Tiger Shot, MK/HK Knee, or spaced Drive Rush normals; a successful Throw Escape builds 1 Drive bar and 1000 Super gauge (10% bar); Throw Escape is awarded to a random player if input simultaneously

Sagat.name: Back Taunt
Sagat.notes: "If you're on a path to attain strength, show me your worth!"

Sagat.name: Standing Heavy Kick
Sagat.notes: Upper Body/Leg hurtbox is anti-air invincible on frames 9-15 (solid anti-air against midrange jumps); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit forces stand on hit; 2nd hit whiffs on crouching opponents (2f worse on block); 4f extra recovery if both hits whiff; 1st hit deals extra hitstun, allowing a natural combo into 214HK; deals full damage / Drive damage / Meter gain even if only the 2nd hit connects; 1st hit puts airborne opponents into a free juggle state (limited juggle if comboed from a wallsplat or airborne crumple), then air resets on the 2nd hit; 2nd hit only has juggle potential after the 1st hit connects; the first 11 recovery frames extend a wide leg hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by standing normals; carries counter-hit/Punish Counter advantage through both hits

Sagat.name: Standing Heavy Punch
Sagat.notes: 3f extra recovery on whiff; huge range poke with a hitconfirmable TC follow-up; the first 10 recovery frames extend a wide arm-height hurtbox making it easily whiff punished by standing normals

Sagat.name: Tiger Sting
Sagat.notes: Both hits are always a true blockstring; hitconfirmable knockdown from a very strong midrange poke; sets up a KD +42 safe jump when juggled into (like after a DI wallsplat on hit/block)

Sagat.name: Standing Light Kick
Sagat.notes: Long range but slow startup (more comparable to a medium normal); 2f extra recovery on whiff; great whiff punish tool that combos consistently into 623HP on Punish Counter; input overlap with 6LK Step Low Kick makes it harder to walk forward and poke in neutral; DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame

Sagat.name: Standing Light Punch
Sagat.notes: Chains into 5LP/2LP/2LK; great range for a chainable 5f jab (but slightly shorter than a standard shoto 5LK); DR cancel is delayed until after 2nd recovery frame; Sagat's only light normal that combos naturally into 214LK

Sagat.name: Standing Medium Kick
Sagat.notes: Very long poke with a semi-hitconfirmable TC follow-up; more range vs. standing opponents (the tip of the hitbox whiffs on crouching opponents); the first 10 recovery frames extend a wide leg hurtbox making it more easily whiff punished by standing normals

Sagat.name: Step Middle Kick
Sagat.notes: 3f blockstring gap between hits; somewhat hitconfirmable knockdown from a very strong midrange poke; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (can combo 623LP after DI wallsplat on hit)

Sagat.name: Standing Medium Punch
Sagat.notes: Core pressure tool for frame traps (5MPx2 sets up a trade combo vs. most reversal 4f normals); pushback on block is too far for a throw mixup without Drive Rush; links consistently into 2MP on counter-hit or into 5HK on Punish Counter (very strong Drive Reversal punish option); on regular hit can lead to 5MP, 5MP, 5LP combo

Sagat.name: Neutral Taunt
Sagat.notes: "If you desire the throne, stand tall against the emperor."

Sagat.name: Tiger Uppercut
Sagat.notes: Extremely long range but slow startup (cannot combo naturally from light normals, but works well as a combo ender from 5LK whiff punish); deals 600 less damage on active frames 3-10; cannot hit cross-up; can be charged into a much stronger version by holding the button 24 frames; releasing the button early results in uncharged 623HP with 8f startup after release; if partially charged, the Air Invuln is 1-9f then 1-11f after the button is released, and the airborne frames are 12-57f after the button is released; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

Sagat.name: Tiger Uppercut (hold)
Sagat.notes: Button must be held 24f for fully charged version; causes a wall splat on hit that leaves Sagat at a fixed distance (no follow-up combo); deals 1100 less damage on active frames 4-10 with no wallsplat animation (KD +29 on active frame 4); cannot hit cross-up; 1st hit puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-3 only)

Sagat.name: Tiger Uppercut
Sagat.notes: Sagat's primary anti-air with fast startup but short range; deals 300 less damage on active frames 4-10; cannot hit cross-up; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

Sagat.name: Tiger Uppercut
Sagat.notes: Much more range than LP version for mid-range anti airs and more consistent cancels from light normals; much slower startup (limits usefulness in many juggles); forward movement makes Sagat more likely to whiff under an opponent's jump-in; deals 600 less damage on active frames 4-10; cannot hit cross-up; puts opponent into a limited juggle state (allows SA3 cancel on active frames 1-2 only)

Sagat.name: Tiger Uppercut
Sagat.notes: Sagat's main reversal; slightly slower than most OD reversals (can be safejabbed by Dee Jay 5LP but is otherwise reliable); deals less damage if it connects on later active frames (1st hit deals significant portion of overall damage); cannot hit cross-up

Sagat.name: Step High Kick
